articles.title: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Query clarification is essential for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that face ambiguous user queries. We consider multi-turn grounded conversational scenarios where a user query is either ill-formed or ambiguous in the context of the prior dialog or, more interestingly, it may be well-formed but when posed against retrieved documents there are multiple relevant interpretations. articles.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. articles.title: SpecEvo: Speculative Evolution with Large Language Models for Cost-Efficient Scientific Discovery
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-driven evolutionary search is a promising paradigm for scientific discovery, but existing methods remain costly and slow, often applying expensive reasoning uniformly while underusing evidence from failed, redundant, and saturated trials. articles.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. articles.title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic harness evolution optimizes an agent's instructions, tools, and control flow by using its task execution experiences as evolving evidence. While more evolution tasks should intuitively improve performance, our preliminary study reveals a paradoxical failure mode: the performance of existing methods degrades as the task pool expands. articles.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated judges of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) outputs are necessary, but large language model (LLM) judges are costly and slow at scale.
